entries.clue: Employment à la Ubers – or horse-drawn carriages? (3,7)

blocks.note: work in short paid jobs, as Uber drivers do
a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, so a whole economy of them, whimsically

annotation.surface: A wry comparison between modern ride-hailing work and the cabbies of the horse-drawn age.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: GIG here is the old carriage, not a short job.
annotation.definitionFit: The gig economy is the labour market of short-term freelance jobs, typified by Uber drivers.

entries.clue: Drop golf ball that’s been lifted high (4)

blocks.note: Golf is G in the NATO alphabet
a lob is a ball hit high in the air

annotation.surface: A golfer being told to drop a ball after it has been skied into trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drop' reads as the golf verb for taking a penalty drop, but it is a noun: a drop of liquid.
annotation.definitionFit: A glob is a small drop or lump of something liquid or semi-liquid.

entries.clue: Jerk, English in French holiday home (4)

blocks.note: git is British slang for an unpleasant or stupid person, a jerk
E is the standard abbreviation for English

annotation.surface: An obnoxious English tourist staying in a rented French cottage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction but only joins the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A gîte is a furnished holiday home in France, usually rented to tourists.

entries.clue: Where youngsters’ habits may be unpleasant? (8,4)

annotation.definition: Where youngsters’ habits may be unpleasant?

blocks.note: the surface pushes behaviour children pick up; a habit is also a garment, here a baby's nappy
the surface suggests bad manners; the setter means a soiled nappy being swapped

annotation.surface: A worry about where children pick up bad habits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Habits' reads as behaviour, but it is clothing, as in a nun's or riding habit: the soiled nappy being swapped.
annotation.definitionFit: Changing mats are the padded mats on which babies are laid to have their nappies changed.

entries.clue: Mostly unwelcome sound: O, Everyman is most unwelcome! (7)

indicatorNotes.Mostly: most of the word, so drop its last letter

blocks.note: NOISE, an unwelcome sound, minus its last letter
the letter as printed
the setter refers to himself, so Everyman is ME

annotation.surface: The setter cheerfully admitting he is a thoroughly unwelcome noise.
annotation.walkthrough: Setters often use their own pseudonym for ME, as here with Everyman.
annotation.definitionFit: Noisome means extremely offensive or disagreeable, especially of a smell: most unwelcome.

entries.clue: Least brief amount of time? I’m … I’m not sure (7)

blocks.note: min is the short form of minute
taken as printed
um is the noise of hesitation

annotation.surface: A hesitant speaker trying to work out the smallest possible amount of time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brief' does double work: it abbreviates minute to MIN. The first 'I’m' is taken literally; the second trails into the uncertain UM.
annotation.definitionFit: Minimum as an adjective means least, the smallest possible.

entries.clue: House detective, part employed (4)

indicatorNotes.part: only part of the following words is taken

blocks.note: hoUSE Detective

annotation.surface: A hotel or store detective who is only employed part-time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part employed' reads as a job arrangement; 'part' actually points into the letters of 'House detective'.
annotation.definitionFit: Used means employed, as in 'the tools employed'.

entries.clue: Horse that provides sustenance in the main (10)

annotation.definition2: that provides sustenance in the main

blocks.note: a champion American racehorse of the 1930s

blocks.clueFragment: that provides sustenance in the main
blocks.note: 'the main' is the sea; the hard dry ship's bread sailors lived on

annotation.surface: A horse that mostly supplies food, or a mainly nourishing animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly', but the main is the sea, where sailors lived on sea biscuit; Seabiscuit was also a famous racehorse.
annotation.definitionFit: Seabiscuit was a celebrated racehorse, and sea biscuit is ship's bread for sailors.

entries.clue: More like preliminary version, read aloud and increasingly windy? (10)

indicatorNotes.read aloud: says to go by the sound of the word, not its spelling

blocks.note: a draft is a preliminary version, so more draft-like is 'draftier'

annotation.surface: A document that becomes rougher and more long-winded when read out.
annotation.walkthrough: British English spells a current of air 'draught' but a rough version 'draft'; the two sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Draughtier means having more draughts of air: windier, by degrees.

entries.clue: Sufferer sedated, calm (10)

blocks.note: knocked out, unconscious
patient = calm, unhurried

annotation.surface: A patient who has been given a sedative and is now calm.
annotation.walkthrough: An outpatient is treated in hospital without staying overnight, so 'sufferer' is a loose but fair definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An outpatient is someone receiving hospital treatment for an ailment, a sufferer.

entries.clue: A sucker rejected some bubbly (4)

indicatorNotes.rejected: sent back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: as printed
a vac is a vacuum cleaner, which sucks

annotation.surface: A mug turning down a glass of fizz.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' suggests a gullible person; it is the vacuum cleaner.
annotation.definitionFit: Cava is Spanish sparkling wine, a kind of bubbly.

entries.clue: Learning, fast, to arrange relatives’ accommodations (7,5)

indicatorNotes.arrange: put the letters into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A quick study sorting out where the extended family will stay.
annotation.walkthrough: A granny flat is a self-contained annexe for an elderly relative, attached to a family home.
annotation.definitionFit: Grannie flats are self-contained living spaces built for older relatives.

entries.clue: Grim, noon, dog barking: you can’t say this now! (4,7)

indicatorNotes.barking: barking mad, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A gloomy midday with a dog yapping, and a greeting that is now out of time.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'noon' in the fodder: at midday it is too late for this greeting. Barking is British slang for mad.
annotation.definitionFit: Good morning is a greeting you can no longer use once it is noon.

entries.clue: Grand! I have beer – and dog returning to offer support (4,1,3,2)

indicatorNotes.returning: going back, so the word runs in reverse

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
I've, contracted
ale is a kind of beer
a pug is a small dog

annotation.surface: Someone delighted to have a pint and their dog coming home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grand!' looks like an exclamation of pleasure; it is G, as in a thousand pounds.
annotation.definitionFit: To give someone a leg up is to help them climb, or to offer support in general.

entries.clue: Spooner’s to provide support for violinists etc (6,4)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: provide = bring; it takes the ST sound from the next word
support = stand, as in a music stand; it takes the B sound from the first word

annotation.surface: A plea on behalf of fiddle players needing backing.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the opening B of BRING with the ST of STAND and you get STRING BAND.
annotation.definitionFit: A string band is a group of players of stringed instruments such as violins.

entries.clue: Exciting under canvas by the sound of it (7)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: says to go by how the words are spoken

blocks.note: under canvas means camping, in tents

annotation.surface: Someone describing a thrilling camping trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Under canvas' is the usual phrase for camping.
annotation.definitionFit: Intense can mean exciting, full of strong feeling.

blocks.note: read as written, a lone preposition with a puzzled question mark
meant as a picture: TOM, a male cat, with its tail (last letter) missing

annotation.walkthrough: A tom is a male cat; lop off its tail and you have TO. The breed from the Isle of Man is famous for having no tail.
annotation.definitionFit: A Manx cat is a breed from the Isle of Man born without a tail.

entries.clue: Twin, having consumed gin, recalled puzzles (7)

indicatorNotes.having consumed: the first word has taken the second inside it
indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so the result runs backwards

blocks.note: twin as an adjective: identical, the same
as printed

annotation.surface: One twin, after a few gins, remembering some riddles.
annotation.walkthrough: SAM(GIN)E, then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an enigma is something baffling, a riddle.

entries.clue: Shepherd who played up front for England? (7)

annotation.definition2: who played up front for England

blocks.note: loosely, a sheep worker: one who clips fleeces

blocks.clueFragment: who played up front for England
blocks.note: Alan, England's centre forward and captain in the 1990s

annotation.surface: A trivia question about a footballer with a pastoral name.
annotation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is the Premier League's all-time top scorer and led England's attack. A sheep shearer is loosely a shepherd.
annotation.definitionFit: A shearer clips the fleece from sheep, a shepherd's task.

entries.clue: Harlequin inexhaustibly portraying some characters: that’s the tonic (7)

indicatorNotes.portraying some characters: shows some of the letters in the words before it

blocks.note: harleQUIN INExhaustibly

annotation.surface: A theatre review praising an actor's tireless comic role.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Portraying some characters' sounds like acting parts; characters are letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Quinine gives tonic water its bitter taste, so it is the tonic in the drink.

entries.clue: Queen in time to introduce Alien V (7)

annotation.definitionNote: V is the Roman numeral five; a quintet is a set of five

blocks.note: QU is an abbreviation for queen
as printed
T for time, as in physics
ET, the film's extraterrestrial

annotation.surface: A queen arriving just in time to open the fifth film in the Alien franchise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alien V' reads as a film sequel title, but it splits: Alien is ET, and V is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A quintet is a group of five, and V is the Roman numeral five.

entries.clue: Comic interlude – but does it describe a darkness? (5,6)

blocks.note: a spell of humour that breaks the tension
taken literally, light relieves darkness

annotation.surface: A critic wondering whether a funny scene suits a grim play.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading: relief from the dark by light.
annotation.definitionFit: Light relief is a humorous break from something serious.

entries.clue: Volcano where the stake’s raised (4)

indicatorNotes.raised: lifted up, so in a down clue the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: an ante is a poker stake

annotation.surface: A gambling den perched on a volcano, where the stakes keep going up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised' suggests raising the bet in poker; in a down answer it turns the word upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sicily's great active volcano.

entries.clue: Primarily, oceanic ravenous creature: aargh! (4)

indicatorNotes.Primarily: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: Oceanic Ravenous Creature Aargh

annotation.surface: A swimmer's scream on spotting a hungry sea beast.
annotation.walkthrough: The words that describe the killer whale also spell it with their initials.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the whole clue is a gasp at a hungry sea predator, which the killer whale is.

entries.clue: 1/28 oz good butter (4)

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

annotation.surface: A recipe measure: a tiny weight of quality butter.
annotation.walkthrough: An ounce is about 28.35 grams, so a gram is roughly a twenty-eighth of one. 'Butter' is the thing that butts, not the dairy spread.
annotation.definitionFit: A gram is about one twenty-eighth of an ounce.

entries.clue: One drawing things out – using this? (10)

blocks.note: someone who prolongs, or protracts, matters
'drawing' again, now in the geometry sense: the instrument you draw angles with

annotation.surface: A question about someone who drags things on, and the tool they use.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawing out' means prolonging; the question mark reuses 'drawing' for the geometry set, where the same word names the angle-measuring tool.
annotation.definitionFit: A protractor is a semicircular instrument for measuring and drawing angles; literally, one who protracts.

entries.clue: Cushions in apartments (4)

blocks.note: soft stuffed pieces for comfort or protection
a pad is slang for a flat or home

annotation.surface: Soft furnishings in a set of flats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction but only links the two meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a soft stuffed cushion, and slang for the place where you live.

entries.clue: Naughty child is on the loo (but only half) somewhere in Slovakia (10)

indicatorNotes.but only half: keep just the first half of the word

blocks.note: a brat is a badly behaved child
as printed
LAVATORY, the loo, cut to its first four of eight letters

annotation.surface: A child misbehaving on the toilet somewhere on a Slovak holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' is the down-clue and across-clue signal that one piece follows another. Loo is British for toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: Bratislava is the capital city of Slovakia, so it is certainly somewhere in Slovakia.
